All the heroes below the wall shouted as one, “Revolt!” A storm of arrows flew toward the battlements. Grand Marshal Gao scarcely managed to dodge out of the way. Troops and cavalry burst out from all four gates. At a single drumbeat from Song Jiang’s army, all his men mounted and fled. The government troops pursued them for some five or six li, then turned back. Just then, a cannon boomed behind them: from the east came Li Kui, leading infantry into the attack; from the west came Hu Sanniang with cavalry, and the two forces converged upon them together. Fearing an ambush, the government troops hastily retreated; but then Song Jiang’s entire band wheeled around and swept back upon them. Assailed from three sides, the city’s forces fell into utter confusion and fled back in haste, suffering many deaths. Song Jiang recalled his troops and forbade further pursuit, then returned to Liangshan Marsh.

p.src: Song Jiang immediately ordered cattle and horses slaughtered and a magnificent banquet prepared. While rewards were distributed among the troops, drums and wind instruments resounded, and every chief, great and small, assembled to meet Grand Marshal Gao. When all had exchanged courtesies, Song Jiang raised a cup of wine, Wu Yong and Gongsun Sheng held the flask and tray, and Lu Junyi and the others stood waiting in attendance. Song Jiang began: “How could a lowly clerk branded upon the face dare rebel against the sacred court? Yet accumulated wrongs and accusations drove me to this pass. Though twice we received imperial grace, the deceptions and abuses that intervened are too numerous to recount in detail. I earnestly beg Your Excellency to take pity on us, rescue those sunk in this deep plight, and let us behold the light of day again. We shall engrave the favor upon our very bones and swear to defend the realm unto death.” Gao Qiu looked upon the host of stalwart men, each fierce and heroic, while Lin Chong and Yang Zhi glared at him as if ready to erupt. Already thoroughly terrified, he said, “Song Gongming, all of you may set your minds at ease! When I return to court, I shall certainly submit a strong memorial, asking that generous imperial mercy and a general pardon be granted, that an offer of amnesty be brought to you, and that you be richly rewarded and raised in office. Then every righteous warrior, high and low, shall enjoy an imperial stipend and become a loyal minister.” Song Jiang was overjoyed to hear this and bowed his thanks to the Grand Marshal. That day’s banquet was conducted with the greatest order and splendor. The chiefs, great and small, took turns offering cups and pressed their guest to drink with the utmost courtesy. Grand Marshal Gao became very drunk. The wine loosened his restraint, and he said, “From childhood I have mastered the art of wrestling, and none beneath heaven can match me.” Lu Junyi was drunk as well. Annoyed by the Grand Marshal’s boast that none beneath heaven could match him, he pointed at Yan Qing and said, “This young brother of mine also knows wrestling. Three times he competed at the wrestling contests on Mount Tai, and none beneath heaven could match him.” Gao Qiu rose at once and stripped off his clothes, intending to wrestle Yan Qing. The chiefs saw that Song Jiang honored him as a grand marshal of the imperial court, so they had been forced to humor him and listen to his boasting. Now, unexpectedly, he meant to compel Yan Qing to wrestle, and they were eager to silence Gao Qiu’s bragging. They all rose and cried, “Good! Good! Let us watch the match!” The whole company surged noisily out of the hall. Song Jiang too was drunk and could no longer decide what to do. The two men stripped off their clothes upon the steps of the hall, and Song Jiang ordered soft mats spread out. Standing upon the close-piled carpet, the two assumed their opening stances. Gao Qiu rushed in. Yan Qing met him deftly, seized him in an unbreakable grip, and with a single throw flipped him onto the mat, where he lay in a heap, unable to struggle up for a long while. This throw was known as the “Life-Preserving Throw.” Song Jiang and Lu Junyi hastily helped Gao Qiu up and dressed him again, saying with smiles, “Your Excellency is drunk; how could you wrestle successfully in such a state? We earnestly beg your pardon!” Gao Qiu was overwhelmed with alarm and humiliation. He returned to the banquet, drank until deep into the night, and was then helped into the rear hall to rest.

p.src: Now Grand Marshal Gao and his party made their way back toward Jizhou, and messengers arrived ahead of them with the news. Zhou Ang, the vanguard commander at Jizhou, together with Wang Huan, Xiang Yuanzhen, Zhang Kai, Prefect Zhang Shuye, and the others, came out of the city to welcome them. Grand Marshal Gao entered the city and stayed for several days while the troops were put in order.
